newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to axe 10,000 military police - report.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to axe 10,000 military police - report.

text.p: Taiwan plans to cut the number of military police by 10,000 as part of the island's plan to cut its armed forces, the China Times newspaper said on Sunday.

The armed forces police command would keep about 15,000 military police after the reduction programme, the newspaper quoted unnamed military sources as saying. It did not say when the reduction would be completed.
In addition, several units and departments under the armed forces police command would be merged or abolished.
Taiwan has said it will cut troop numbers from 453,000 to 400,000 over the next four years, leaving more funds to modernise itself and buy more defensive weapons.

Taiwan and China have been rivals since the sides split at the end of a civil war in 1949. Beijing regards Taiwan as a renegade province to be brought under China's eventual rule, by force if necessary.
